  26. The Ganges is sacred to millions of people.
  27. The Danube flows through ten countries.
  28. The Rhine is a major European shipping route.

  30. The Mekong supports huge inland fisheries.
  31. Waterfalls form where hard rock overlies soft rock.
  32. Rapids mark shallow, rocky, fast stretches. 
  33. Canyons are carved by rivers over long time spans.
  34. The Grand Canyon was cut largely by the Colorado.
  35. Gorges are narrow, steep river valleys.
  36. V-shaped valleys are typical of young rivers.
  37. Braided rivers split into many shifting channels.
  38. Seasonal rivers flow only part of the year.
  39. Rivers move sand, silt, clay and dissolved minerals.
  40. Suspended load clouds the water. 
  41. Bed load rolls and bounces along the bottom.
  42. Discharge is the volume of water passing per second.
  43. Floods happen when discharge exceeds channel capacity.
  44. Dams store water and generate electricity.
  45. Dams also trap sediment and block fish.

  55. Riparian zones are the lands along riverbanks.
  56. Wetlands beside rivers absorb floodwater.
  57. Beavers build dams that reshape small streams.
  58. Rivers supply drinking water to billions.
  59. Irrigation draws heavily on river flow.
  60. Some rivers no longer reach the sea most years.
  61. Pollution from farms and cities harms river life.
  62. Restoration projects remove old dams and reopen channels.
  63. Ice can freeze rivers solid in cold climates.
  64. Ice jams can cause sudden floods in spring.

  66. Rivers recharge and draw from groundwater.
  67. Satellites now track river flow and flooding.
  68. Rivers appear constantly in poetry and song.
  69. Heraclitus said no one steps in the same river twice.
  70. Every river eventually returns its water to the cycle.
